newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ bonds hold onto gains at close on short-squeeze.
newsitem.headline: NZ bonds hold onto gains at close on short-squeeze.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD
10-YR T-BONDS (DEC) 92.60 (UNTRADED) 10-YR 7.47 (-0.16)
OVERNIGHT CASH 9.90 PCT (PREV 9.90) US 30-YR 6.80 (PREV 6.86)
* NZ bonds hold onto morning gains, yields end on lows
* Shortage of stock seen driving yields
* Further volatility seen
New Zealand bonds held onto their morning gains and yields closed on their lows on Friday as the market saw a continuing short squeeze, dealers said.
"Most locals look like they're probably a little short of stock at the moment and fearful of being caught short again. It's a classic short-squeeze, basically," a Wellington trader said.

He said the scramble for stock was the over-riding factor, taking precedence over this week's benign inflation data and the possibility of a centre-right coalition emerging from post-election talks due to start next week.
Nationalist New Zealand First, which holds the balance of power, is due to start talks with both the conservative National Party and the Labour Party but these could drag on for some weeks.

"I kind of feel now that's it's going to be very difficult for people to be buying too much more stock in this market because I think the locals will be very reluctant offerers and they won't get a very good price," the dealer said.

The 7/98 bond dropped 11 points in yield on Thursday and a further 18 on Friday to close at 7.13 percent. The 02/00s finished around 7.48 percent, little changed from their morning levels, while the 10-year bond also held its gains to end at 7.47 percent.

Another dealer commented: "The market is a real lottery. It's bobbing about like a bit of a cork at the moment. It's past fundamental value so it's trading on purely speculative punting on supply and demand."
He said there was still no guarantee the market would run into selling at these levels.
Ninety-day bank bills also rallied, reflecting the strong currency, to end six points lower in yield at 9.58 percent.
